title: Constant coefficient projection maps for ordinary etale system compact supports
statement:
Let $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ have characteristic $p$ and let $\ell\ne p$ be prime [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes, with no separatedness assumption on $Y$, and fix a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p_f}Y$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. For an inverse sequence $C_\bullet$ of finite commutative rings annihilated by powers of $\ell$, write $\mathscr S_C(W)$ for strict systems of $(C_n)_{W_{\mathrm{et}}}$-module sheaves, with $C_{n+1}$-linear transitions $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{C_{n+1}\to C_n}M_n$ and compatible componentwise morphisms, and use its ordinary unbounded derived category and evaluation $e_n$ [lem-pur-system-level-left-extension]. Set $F_C=Rp_{f,C,*}j_{!,C}$ and $F_{C_n}=Rp_{f,*,C_n}j_!$, where open extension and ordinary etale direct image act termwise before derivation [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. 
For any compatible map $a:C_\bullet\to D_\bullet$ of such ring sequences let $T_a^W=-\otimes^L_{C_\bullet}D_\bullet$ and let $U_a^W$ be exact restriction of scalars. The derived tensor/restriction adjunction is the one with unit $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. There are canonical restriction identifications $U_a^YF_D\cong F_CU_a^X$ and canonical natural isomorphisms
$$q_a:T_a^YF_C\xrightarrow{\sim}F_DT_a^X.$$
The coefficient-adjunction transpose of $q_a$ is $F_C$ applied to its scalar unit followed by the inverse restriction identification. At level $n$ this is the ordinary constant-coefficient compact-support projection for $C_n\to D_n$, in the $D_n$-linear derived category. The same assertion holds for a single map of finite rings. No flatness or cohomological bound on the input is required.

These are actual maps of derived systems, natural on derived morphisms and independent of resolutions. Under canonical balanced tensor associators $\tau_W:T_b^WT_a^W\cong T_{ba}^W$, for composable coefficient maps $a,b$ they satisfy
$$q_{ba}\circ\tau_YF_C=F_H\tau_X\circ(q_bT_a^X)\circ T_b^Yq_a,$$
where $H_\bullet$ is the final ring sequence. An identity ring map gives the identity comparison. These identities also hold in mixed quotient/extension diagrams, before evaluation.

proof.text: Construct the normalized ordinary system presentation t using the sequence-site existence lemma. Its functors and comparisons are fixed by actual direct image, adjunction and identity-on-sections normalization; no projection isomorphism is assumed.

The definition of q is the inverse scalar-adjunction mate of the inverse restriction comparison. Mathlib unit_mateEquiv_symm gives exactly the scalar transpose equation, without any new proof obligation.

Use the evaluation-normalization equation. At every level the compact scalar map is invertible: proper_scalarMate_isIso applies to the finite source ring and proper compactification map, and the open scalar comparison is an isomorphism. Every level of q is therefore invertible after cancelling the specified evaluation isomorphisms. The ordinary evaluations jointly reflect isomorphisms since they retain all component section maps; the proof passes through the faithful forgetful functor to presheaves of abelian groups and ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective. Functor.jointlyReflectIsomorphisms_mapDerivedCategory lifts this criterion to the ordinary unbounded derived categories. Hence q is an isomorphism.

The coefficient coherence lemma gives q(a followed by b)=path(a,b) and the unit equation. Rewrite both mixed paths as q of their composites. congr_arg_heq applied to the dependent function sending a coefficient map to q proves the mixed-square assertion from equality of composites.

The single-ring normalization lemma supplies the proper/open restriction isomorphism, the scalar adjunct equation and the coefficient cocycle. The same proper_scalarMate_isIso and open-isomorphism argument proves the single-ring isomorphism clause. These are independent of the finite-field geometry hypotheses and apply to the compactification in the unchanged statement.
